title: Monetary Policy Under Time-Varying Uncertainty Aversion
abstract: The paper develops a framework for studying optimal policy by an inflation-targeting central bank that is uncertain about the structure of the economy and whose degree of uncertainty aversion changes over time. Such shifts can reflect structural breaks or shocks to prices, output, or the real exchange rate. Robust control represents the policymaker’s aversion to model uncertainty, while a Markov chain captures changes in that aversion. The model generally implies a more forceful interest-rate response when uncertainty aversion is higher or is more likely to rise. Greater aversion also lowers the policymaker’s welfare, while the effect of Markov transition probabilities on expected losses is ambiguous.
